matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides (including any addition or subtraction) to know the exact imbalance. Then choose a single‑stick move that can correct that difference.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move.
matchstick.example: A solver moves a stick without first computing the numeric values, resulting in a transformation that does not address the actual imbalance.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and a V appears on the side that must increase, move one of its diagonal sticks to form an X, raising its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the side needing increase contains a V and the difference is 5.
matchstick.example: A solver removes a diagonal from V, leaving a single diagonal, instead of converting V to X to add 5.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that contains at least one I to another numeral that can accept an extra I (e.g., turning V into IV or adding an I to make II), ensuring both source and target remain valid Roman numerals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance matches the value change caused by adding or removing a single I (1).
matchstick.example: A solver takes an I from a solitary I, leaving no numeral, rather than moving it between numerals that can remain valid.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals sign to the minus sign, turning the equals into a minus and the minus into an equals, while keeping both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and the numeric imbalance suggests that swapping them could help.
matchstick.example: A solver swaps '-' and '=', but then fails to check that the new equation still balances numerically, producing an incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Ensure a valid '=' remains when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When taking a horizontal stick away from the equality sign, verify that the remaining single horizontal still forms a valid minus sign; never leave the equality sign without any horizontal sticks.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever you consider moving a stick from the '=' operator.
matchstick.example: A solver removes both horizontals from '=', leaving no operator, which invalidates the equation.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the numeric imbalance is exactly 5 and an X appears on the side that must decrease, move one of its diagonal sticks to break the X into a V, reducing its value by 5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the side needing reduction contains an X and the difference is 5.
matchstick.example: A solver removes a diagonal from X, leaving a single diagonal that is not a valid numeral, instead of converting X to V to subtract 5.

matchstick.title: Evaluate expressions when computing numeric imbalance
matchstick.principle: Fully evaluate any arithmetic expressions (e.g., addition, subtraction) on each side before comparing numeric values, so that the imbalance reflects the true result of the expression.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation contains operators like '+' or '-'.
matchstick.example: A solver compares the raw numerals without evaluating the addition or subtraction, miscalculating the numeric imbalance.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality
matchstick.principle: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 2, move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the side with excess to a numeral on the other side, adjusting both sides by 1 each and preserving equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is 2 and both sides contain numerals that can lose or gain a single I.
matchstick.example: A solver moves an I from a numeral that cannot lose it (e.g., a solitary I), breaking the source numeral.

matchstick.title: Reposition I before X to change XI to IX
matchstick.principle: If a numeral 'XI' appears, moving its I‑stick to the left of the X changes it to 'IX', decreasing its value by 2.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the side needing reduction contains the pattern XI and the imbalance matches the 2‑unit change.
matchstick.example: A solver moves the I from XI to another location, leaving an invalid X or I, rather than repositioning it to form IX.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: If a '+' operator is present and a V numeral appears on the side that must increase by 1, you can move the vertical stick from '+' to the left of the V, turning V into IV and '+' into '-', yielding a valid equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and a V that needs to become IV (increase by 1) to balance the numeric difference.
matchstick.example: A solver removes the vertical stick from '+' but places it on a numeral that cannot accept a vertical stick, creating an invalid numeral.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats any stick as removable without checking whether the source numeral would still be a legal Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Before removing a stick, verify that the source numeral remains a valid Roman numeral after the removal.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the move itself and neglects the overall syntactic and semantic validity of the resulting expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After performing the stick move, re‑parse the whole equation to ensure every symbol is a valid Roman numeral or operator.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid '=' sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any horizontal can be taken from '=', not recognizing that at least one horizontal must remain to form a minus sign.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you take a stick from '=', ensure exactly one horizontal remains so it becomes a valid '-' operator.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after finding a syntactically correct arrangement and forgets to recompute the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always recompute the numeric values of both sides after the move and confirm they are equal before outputting the answer.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes interprets a transformation as needing two separate adjustments and performs both.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Constrain the reasoning to a single stick relocation; any change to a symbol must be explained as moving exactly one line segment.
